definition: careful to avoid danger or mistakes

hero.text: Juniper was cautious on the icy rooftop, testing each step before putting her weight down.

everyday: Grandpa is cautious at the busy corner and looks both ways twice before crossing.

contrast.nonExample: Theo raced down the steep hill on his bike without touching the brakes.
contrast.explanation: Cautious people slow down and think about danger first. Theo rushed ahead without any care, so he was reckless, not cautious.

items.prompt: Which person is being cautious?

options.text: Mila taps the pond ice with a stick before stepping on it.
Jon dashes straight onto the frozen pond without looking first or checking.
Ana laughs as she slides across the pond.

items.hint: Look for the person who checks for danger first.
items.explanation: Cautious means careful to avoid danger. Mila tests the ice before she trusts it.

wrong.b: Jon does not check at all, so he is careless, not cautious.
wrong.c: Ana is having fun, but nothing shows she is being careful.

items.prompt: Choose the word that best completes the sentence.
items.passage: Mom is ___ with hot pans, so she always uses thick oven mitts.
items.hint: Why would someone always wear thick mitts?
items.explanation: "Always uses thick oven mitts" shows Mom is careful not to get burned. That is cautious.

items.prompt: Which word means the OPPOSITE of "cautious" in this sentence?
items.passage: The cautious hiker stayed far away from the edge of the cliff.
items.hint: The opposite of being careful about danger is...?
items.explanation: Reckless means not caring about danger, the opposite of cautious. Careful means the same as cautious, not the opposite.

wrong.a: Careful is a synonym of cautious, not its opposite.

items.prompt: Build a sentence that shows what cautious means.
items.hint: A cautious person is careful. Which ending shows care?
items.explanation: Taking small, slow steps on a wet floor is careful, so it shows caution. Running and sliding is careless.

items.prompt: Which word best describes Lily?
items.passage: Before she touched the strange plant, Lily put on gloves and asked her teacher if it was safe.
items.clue: put on gloves; asked her teacher if it was safe
items.hint: What does Lily do before she touches the plant?
items.explanation: Lily "put on gloves" and "asked if it was safe" before touching anything. Checking for danger first is being cautious.

definition: lucky; having something good happen to you

hero.text: Bolt was fortunate that the storm stopped just as he finished fixing the bridge.

everyday: We were fortunate to get a sunny day for our class picnic.

contrast.nonExample: Ella practiced every single day, so she earned a spot on the soccer team.
contrast.explanation: Fortunate means something good happens by luck. Ella earned her spot through hard work, so it was not just luck.

items.prompt: Is Max fortunate?
items.passage: Max dropped his ice cream cone, but it landed right side up on a clean plate.
items.hint: Did something lucky happen to Max?
items.explanation: Fortunate means lucky. The cone landing safely on a clean plate was a lucky break for Max.

items.prompt: Choose the word that best completes the sentence.
items.passage: Our bus was late, but we were ___ because the show had not started yet.
items.clue: the show had not started yet
items.hint: Being late could have been bad. What happened instead?
items.explanation: "The show had not started yet" means things worked out by luck even though the bus was late. That is fortunate.

items.prompt: Which word is closest in meaning to "fortunate" in this sentence?
items.passage: Nia felt fortunate to find her lost key in the tall grass.
items.hint: Finding a tiny key in tall grass takes some luck.
items.explanation: Lucky means the same as fortunate. Clever would mean she found it by being smart, but the sentence is about good luck.

items.prompt: Build a sentence that shows what fortunate means.

chunks.text: because he lost his lunch money

items.hint: Fortunate means something lucky happened. Which reason is lucky?
items.explanation: Finding a dollar is a lucky surprise, so Sam was fortunate. Losing money is unlucky.

items.prompt: The prefix un- means "not." What does "unfortunate" mean in this sentence?
items.passage: It was unfortunate that rain cancelled our baseball game.
items.hint: Un- + fortunate = not ___.
items.explanation: Un- means not, so unfortunate means not lucky. A cancelled game is bad luck.

wrong.a: Lucky is what fortunate means. The un- flips it to the opposite.

definition: wanting to know or learn about something

hero.text: Pixel was curious about the glowing rock, so she studied it under her magnifier.

everyday: The curious toddler opened every kitchen drawer to see what was inside.

contrast.nonExample: Leo yawned and looked away when his friend showed him the new fish tank.
contrast.explanation: Curious people want to find out more. Leo showed no interest at all, so he was bored, not curious.

items.prompt: What does "curious" mean in this sentence?
items.passage: Jada was curious about how bees make honey.

options.text: afraid that something will hurt you

items.hint: Jada is wondering HOW bees do something.
items.explanation: Curious means wanting to know more. Jada wonders how bees make honey, so she wants to learn.

items.prompt: Choose the word that best completes the sentence.
items.passage: The ___ puppy sniffed the new box to find out what was inside.
items.clue: to find out what was inside
items.hint: The puppy wants to find something out.
items.explanation: "To find out what was inside" shows the puppy wants to know something. That is curious.

items.prompt: Which word means the OPPOSITE of "curious" in this sentence?
items.passage: The curious students asked the zookeeper many questions about the snakes.
items.hint: Curious students ask lots of questions. What kind of students would ask none?
items.explanation: Bored students don't care to learn more, the opposite of curious. Interested is a synonym, not an opposite.

wrong.a: Interested means almost the same as curious.

items.prompt: Which line uses "curious" correctly?

options.text: "I'm curious about what's in that box. Can we open it?"
"I'm so curious that I never want to know what is inside it."
"I felt curious, so I went right to sleep."

items.hint: A curious person wants to find out more.
items.explanation: Wanting to open the box to see what's inside shows curiosity. Not wanting to know, or going to sleep, shows no curiosity.

items.prompt: Which word best describes Omar?
items.passage: Omar kept asking questions about the moon and checked out five library books about space.
items.clue: kept asking questions; checked out five library books
items.hint: What do all those questions and books tell you about Omar?
items.explanation: "Kept asking questions" and "five library books about space" show Omar wants to learn more. That is curious.

definition: to say what you think will happen before it happens

hero.text: Kai looked at the dark clouds and predicted the storm would reach the city by noon.

everyday: Before reading the story, our class predicted that the fox would trick the hen.

contrast.nonExample: After the game was over, Ty told everyone the final score.
contrast.explanation: To predict, you tell what will happen BEFORE it happens. Ty reported the score after the game, so he did not predict it.

items.prompt: Which person is predicting?

options.text: Zara says, "I think the ice cube will melt in ten minutes."
Zara says, "The ice cube melted while we sat and watched it."
Zara says, "The ice cube feels cold and wet."

items.hint: Who talks about something that has not happened yet?
items.explanation: To predict is to say what will happen before it does. "Will melt" is about the future.

wrong.b: "Melted" already happened, so Zara is telling what she saw, not predicting.
wrong.c: Zara is describing how it feels right now.

items.prompt: The prefix pre- means "before," and dict means "say." What does "predict" mean?

options.text: to say something so loudly that all can hear
to say what will happen before it happens
to repeat what someone else just said
to write down every word very carefully

items.hint: Put the parts together: say + before.
items.explanation: Pre- (before) + dict (say) = to say before. When you predict, you say what will happen before it happens.

items.prompt: Choose the word that best completes the sentence.
items.passage: Can you ___ what will happen if we leave the ice cream in the sun?
items.hint: The question asks about something in the future.
items.explanation: "What will happen" asks you to think ahead. Saying what will happen before it does is predicting.

items.prompt: Build a sentence that shows what predict means.

chunks.text: that the gray turtle would win.
that the gray turtle had already won.

items.hint: A prediction is about what WILL happen.
items.explanation: "Would win" talks about the future, which is a prediction. "Had already won" can't be true before the race even started.

items.prompt: Which word best names what the weather reporter did?
items.passage: The weather reporter studied the maps and told viewers that snow would fall tomorrow.
items.hint: Is the reporter talking about the past or the future?
items.explanation: "Would fall tomorrow" is about the future, so the reporter predicted. Recalled means remembered something from the past.

definition: wanting very much to do or have something

hero.text: Rex was eager to try his new jet boots and was the first one out the door.

everyday: The eager students raised their hands before the teacher even finished the question.

contrast.nonExample: Ben dragged his feet and walked as slowly as he could on the way to the dentist.
contrast.explanation: Eager means you really want to do something. Ben moved slowly because he did not want to go, so he was reluctant.

items.prompt: Is Lucy eager for the field trip?
items.passage: Lucy packed her bag the night before the field trip and woke up extra early.
items.hint: Does Lucy seem to really want to go?
items.explanation: Packing early and waking up early show Lucy really wants to go. That is eager.

items.prompt: Choose the word that best completes the sentence.
items.passage: The dog was ___ to go for a walk and waited by the door with its leash.
items.clue: waited by the door with its leash
items.hint: What does waiting by the door with a leash show?
items.explanation: "Waited by the door with its leash" shows the dog really wanted to go. That is eager.

items.prompt: Which word means the OPPOSITE of "eager" in this sentence?
items.passage: Tom was eager to share his science project with the class.
items.hint: Look for a word that means NOT wanting to do it.
items.explanation: Reluctant means not wanting to, the opposite of eager. Excited and ready are close to eager.

wrong.b: Excited is close to eager, not opposite.
wrong.c: Ready is close to eager, not opposite.

items.prompt: Build a sentence that shows what eager means.

chunks.text: so she hid in her room.

items.hint: An eager person can't wait. Which ending shows that?
items.explanation: Sitting down early shows Maya couldn't wait to start. Hiding in her room shows she didn't want to go.

items.prompt: Which word best describes Jamal?
items.passage: Jamal couldn't wait to open his new paints and kept asking when he could start.
items.clue: couldn't wait; kept asking when he could start
items.hint: How does Jamal feel about starting?
items.explanation: "Couldn't wait" and "kept asking when he could start" show Jamal really wanted to paint. That is eager.

definition: shy and easily frightened; not brave

hero.text: The timid kitten hid behind Nova's boots until she spoke to it softly.

everyday: On the first day of school, the timid new boy spoke in a tiny whisper.

contrast.nonExample: Grace walked right up to the new students and introduced herself with a big smile.
contrast.explanation: Timid people are shy or easily scared. Grace was bold and friendly, the opposite of timid.

items.prompt: Which animal is timid?

options.text: A rabbit freezes and hides when a leaf falls nearby.
A big dog runs up and barks loudly at every person.
A cat stretches out in the warm sun.

items.hint: Which animal gets scared very easily?
items.explanation: Timid means easily frightened. The rabbit hides from something as small as a falling leaf.

wrong.b: The dog is bold and loud, the opposite of timid.
wrong.c: The cat is relaxed, not frightened.

items.prompt: Choose the word that best completes the sentence.
items.passage: The ___ girl hid behind her mom when the clown said hello.
items.hint: Why might a child hide when someone says hello?
items.explanation: "Hid behind her mom" shows the girl was shy and a little scared. That is timid.

items.prompt: Which word is closest in meaning to "timid" in this sentence?
items.passage: The timid deer ran away at the smallest sound.
items.hint: Why would a deer run from a tiny sound?
items.explanation: Fearful means easily scared, like timid. The deer might be fast too, but running at the smallest sound shows fear.

wrong.c: The deer may be fast, but timid is about being easily scared, not speed.

items.prompt: Build a sentence that shows what timid means.
items.hint: Timid people are shy. Which choice is shy?
items.explanation: Speaking softly around new people is shy, so it shows timid. Shouting hello to everyone is bold.

items.prompt: Which word best describes Ella?
items.passage: Ella wanted to join the game at recess, but she felt too shy and scared to ask.
items.clue: too shy and scared to ask
items.hint: What stops Ella from asking?
items.explanation: "Too shy and scared to ask" shows Ella is timid. She wants to play but feels afraid.

definition: to watch something carefully to learn about it

hero.text: Juniper observed the robot from the rooftop for an hour to learn how it moved.

everyday: In science class, we observed a caterpillar every day as it turned into a butterfly.

contrast.nonExample: Jake glanced at the clock for one second and kept running down the hall.
contrast.explanation: To observe is to watch carefully, often for a while, to learn something. A one-second look is not careful watching.

items.prompt: Is Rosa observing the birds?
items.passage: Rosa sat quietly by the bird feeder for twenty minutes, writing down which birds came.
items.hint: Is Rosa watching carefully to learn something?
items.explanation: Rosa watches closely for a long time and writes down what she sees. That is observing.

items.prompt: Choose the word that best completes the sentence.
items.passage: Scientists ___ the frogs closely to learn what they eat.
items.hint: How do scientists learn about animals?
items.explanation: "Closely" and "to learn" show careful watching. That is observing.

wrong.b: Imitate means copy. Scientists learn by watching the frogs, not copying them.

items.prompt: Which word is closest in meaning to "observe" in this sentence?
items.passage: Please observe how the colors mix when I add water to the paint.
items.hint: What should you do with your eyes while the colors mix?
items.explanation: Watch is closest to observe here. Ignore is the opposite, and guess means you don't look at all.

items.prompt: Build a sentence that shows what observe means.

chunks.text: and drew how its shape changed.
without ever looking up at it.

items.hint: Observing means looking carefully. Which ending fits?
items.explanation: Drawing how the moon's shape changed shows careful watching. You can't observe something without looking at it.

items.prompt: Which line uses "observe" correctly?

options.text: "I will observe the ball by kicking it into the goal."
"Let's observe the ants and see where they go."
"Keep your eyes shut tight while you observe the picture on the wall."

items.hint: Observing means watching carefully.
items.explanation: Watching the ants to see where they go is observing. Kicking is not watching, and you can't observe with your eyes shut.

definition: to tell what something is like using words

hero.text: Pixel described the missing dog to Bolt: small, brown, with one white ear.

everyday: Can you describe your favorite meal so well that I can almost taste it?

contrast.nonExample: Mia pointed at the puppy without saying a word.
contrast.explanation: To describe is to use words to tell what something is like. Pointing shows where it is but gives no details.

items.prompt: Which person is describing something?

options.text: Ivy says her kite is red and diamond-shaped, with a long tail.
Ivy runs across the field and flies her kite high in the windy sky.
Ivy buys a kite at the store.

items.hint: Who uses words to tell what something looks like?
items.explanation: Describing means telling what something is like. Ivy tells the kite's color, shape, and tail.

wrong.b: Ivy is flying the kite, not telling what it is like.
wrong.c: Buying a kite is not using words to tell about it.

items.prompt: Choose the word that best completes the sentence.
items.passage: Use three adjectives to ___ the ocean in your poem.
items.hint: Adjectives are describing words.
items.explanation: Adjectives tell what something is like, so you use them to describe the ocean.

items.prompt: Which words are closest in meaning to "describe" in this sentence?
items.passage: Will you describe the house where you grew up?
items.hint: The person is asking you to use words.
items.explanation: To describe the house is to tell about it in words: its rooms, colors, and yard.

items.prompt: Build a sentence that shows what describe means.

chunks.text: about the loud thunder and bright flashes.
nothing at all on her paper.

items.hint: Describing uses details. Which ending gives details?
items.explanation: Writing about the loud thunder and bright flashes tells what the storm was like. Writing nothing describes nothing.

items.prompt: What is the officer asking the person to do?
items.passage: The officer asked, "What did the thief look like? Tell me his height, hair, and clothes."
items.clue: What did the thief look like? Tell me
items.hint: The officer wants to know what the thief was like.
items.explanation: "What did the thief look like? Tell me..." asks the person to use words to tell details. That is describing.

definition: to look at how two or more things are alike and different

hero.text: Kai compared the two footprints in the mud and saw that one was much bigger.

everyday: In math, we compared the two numbers to see which one was greater.

contrast.nonExample: Lily looked at one apple and said it was red.
contrast.explanation: Comparing needs at least two things. Lily only described one apple, so she did not compare.

items.prompt: Is Jack comparing?
items.passage: Jack held up one leaf and counted the points around its edge.
items.hint: How many leaves is Jack looking at?
items.explanation: To compare, you need two or more things. Jack studies only one leaf, so he is not comparing.

items.prompt: Choose the word that best completes the sentence.
items.passage: Let's ___ the two maps to see which road is shorter.
items.clue: the two maps; which road is shorter
items.hint: You are looking at two things to find a difference.
items.explanation: "The two maps" and "which road is shorter" mean looking at how they differ. That is comparing.

items.prompt: What does "compared" mean in this sentence?
items.passage: The coach compared the two runners' times.

options.text: cheered loudly for each runner in the race
wrote down each time on a chart
looked at how the times were alike or different

items.hint: What do you do with two things when you compare them?
items.explanation: Comparing means looking at how things are alike and different, like which runner was faster.

items.prompt: Build a sentence that shows what compare means.

chunks.text: she saw that one had more chips.
she looked at only one of them.

items.hint: Comparing means finding a difference or sameness between things.
items.explanation: Seeing that one cookie had more chips is a difference found by comparing. Looking at only one cookie is not comparing.

items.prompt: Which word best tells what Ben did?
items.passage: Ben made a chart showing how frogs and toads are the same and how they are different.
items.clue: how they are the same and how they are different
items.hint: Ben looks at two animals side by side.
items.explanation: "The same" and "different" are the two parts of comparing. Ben compared frogs and toads.

definition: very, very old; from a long, long time ago

hero.text: Rex found an ancient map in the museum that was thousands of years old.

everyday: Ancient Egyptians built the pyramids more than four thousand years ago.

contrast.nonExample: Dad's car is ten years old and has a few scratches.
contrast.explanation: Ancient means extremely old, often thousands of years. Ten years is old for a car, but it is not ancient.

items.prompt: Which thing is ancient?

options.text: a clay pot made 3,000 years ago

items.hint: Which one is from the longest time ago?
items.explanation: Ancient means very, very old. A pot from 3,000 years ago is ancient.

items.prompt: Choose the word that best completes the sentence.
items.passage: The ___ castle was built more than a thousand years ago.
items.clue: more than a thousand years ago
items.hint: Look at how long ago the castle was built.
items.explanation: "More than a thousand years ago" tells you the castle is extremely old. That is ancient.

items.prompt: Which word means the OPPOSITE of "ancient" in this sentence?
items.passage: Scientists studied the ancient bones of a dinosaur.
items.hint: Ancient is about age. Which word is about age?
items.explanation: Ancient means very old, so new is the opposite. Huge, broken, and heavy describe size or condition, not age.

items.prompt: Build a sentence that shows what ancient means.
items.hint: Ancient things are very, very old.
items.explanation: Two thousand years makes the tree ancient. A tree that started growing last spring is young.

items.prompt: Which word best describes the coin?
items.passage: Ms. Lee showed us a coin from Rome that people used about 2,000 years ago.
items.hint: How old is the coin?
items.explanation: "About 2,000 years ago" shows the coin is extremely old, so it is ancient.
